stage1_gates.question: Does the project reasonably fit the theme: an application that meaningfully uses BOTH PayPal (developer platform, sandbox) AND an AI tool/model/platform, with PayPal integration central (not a bolt-on pay button)?
Does the project reasonably apply the required PayPal APIs/SDKs (REST APIs, JS SDK, Agent Toolkit, MCP, or other PayPal services) in working code, using the sandbox environment?
Can a judge actually run or interact with a working build via complete setup/run instructions OR a hosted demo URL (not a mockup, static prototype or non-functional demo)?
Is there a GitHub repository containing all source, assets and instructions, with an open-source license file?
Is there a demo video plan/transcript under 3 minutes that shows the project functioning on its platform, intended for public YouTube, without third-party trademarks or copyrighted music?
Do the text description and video only claim features that the code/demo actually implements (Rules: must function as depicted)?

criteria.name: Technological Implementation
criteria.official: How thoroughly and skillfully does the project use PayPal Developer Platform and AI tool(s)? Does the project reflect genuine effort and a working, non-trivial implementation?

anchors.10: >=4 distinct PayPal capabilities used correctly in sandbox with OAuth caching, webhook signature verification, idempotency, pagination and error handling; AI is load-bearing with calibrated confidence and human-in-the-loop; tests and evals present; runs from README quickly.
anchors.7: 2-3 PayPal capabilities wired end-to-end; AI meaningful; some rough edges.
anchors.4: A single PayPal button or API call; AI is a bolted-on chat box.
anchors.1: Mock data only; PayPal not actually called.

criteria.name: Design
criteria.official: Does the project deliver a complete, coherent product experience — not just a technical proof of concept?

anchors.10: Feels like a product: onboarding, main loop, review, reports; empty/loading/error states; consistent visual system; every screen has a purpose.
anchors.7: Coherent main flow; some unpolished screens.
anchors.4: Developer console or raw JSON output.
anchors.1: A script or proof of concept.

criteria.name: Potential Impact
criteria.official: Does the project make a credible, specific case for solving a real problem for a real audience — and does the solution actually address that problem based on what's demonstrated?

anchors.10: Specific audience, quantified pain with sources or measurements, and the demo shows the pain removed with concrete numbers.

criteria.name: Innovation/Idea
criteria.official: How creative and novel is the concept and does the project differ from existing concepts?

anchors.10: Clearly new approach judges haven't seen; differentiated from existing products (e.g., QuickBooks/Xero/PayPal reports) in a way that matters.
anchors.7: Known idea with a meaningful novel twist.

criteria.name: Presentation
criteria.official: Does the video clearly demonstrate the project working end-to-end? Does the pitch communicate what problem is solved, who it's for, and why it matters? Is the overall presentation easy to follow?

anchors.10: Under 2:50; first 15s state who/pain/solution; live end-to-end run in PayPal sandbox; clear narration and captions; ends with impact numbers and architecture.
anchors.7: Clear but slow start or partial flow.
anchors.1: Over 3 minutes, not public, or not on YouTube.

sponsor.AG Grid: Polish: custom widgets, theming, layout tools, not just AG Grid or AG Charts on their own; Studio Agent Framework (custom agent talking to Studio's built-in agents, or swapped-in harness).
sponsor.APIMatic: Uses APIMatic tools (e.g., Context Plugins) to build the PayPal integration.
sponsor.Bryntum: Best use of Gantt, Scheduler and/or Calendar (timeline, resource booking, or an agent that drives the schedule).
sponsor.Channel3: Calls the Channel3 API/MCP meaningfully (search, enrichment, recommendations).

prizes.stacking_rule: Max one Grand + one Sponsor, OR one Honorable Mention + one Sponsor.

personas.title: PayPal Developer Advocate
personas.lens: Idiomatic, correct PayPal integration; developer experience; README clarity; would I show this to the community?

personas.title: PayPal Software Engineer / Engineering Manager
personas.lens: Correct API usage, webhooks verification, idempotency, error handling, security, architecture, reliability.

personas.title: PayPal Senior Product Manager
personas.lens: Real user, real problem, coherent product, business case, differentiation, would merchants adopt it?

personas.title: AG Grid community lead
personas.lens: Polished dashboard, custom widgets, theming, layout, Studio Agent Framework usage, overall UX.

personas.title: Skeptical automated AI reviewer
personas.lens: Penalize unverifiable claims, hype, mockups, AI that is not load-bearing, and anything the evidence doesn't demonstrate.
